parsed.explanation: No documented trans-specific criminal offence, no recorded police targeting, and no documented border detention or screening on gender-marker grounds. Same-sex conduct is legal, and a local indigenous third-gender tradition is documented as normal. Against this, there is no hate-crime recognition or effective anti-discrimination remedy, the 2024 amendment was blocked, public opinion is strongly opposed to same-sex marriage (78% in 2017, 12% approval in 2023), and religious opposition is organised. Visitor-facing exposure is largely open: no facility statute was found, but no visitor-specific data on refusals, violence or custody placement exists. Resident-facing gaps (blood donation, conversion therapy, employment and housing protections) are discounted. Marriage non-recognition is a tangential LGB signal, though it touches a visitor whose relationship would be read as same-sex. Extrapolating from the lack of criminalisation and the absence of documented targeting against the hostile climate and missing recourse gives a reduced-to-elevated rating.
